title: Lift specified local free presentations to quasi-coherent Zariski cokernels
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $c_X$ its canonical Zariski/etale module context [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections], $G$ any small etale module, and $(U_i)$ any family of etale charts [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], without a covering hypothesis. For small $K_i,J_i$, suppose $d_i:\mathcal O_{U_i,et}^{(K_i)}\to\mathcal O_{U_i,et}^{(J_i)}$ and $q_i:\mathcal O_{U_i,et}^{(J_i)}\to G|_{U_i}$ form cokernel coforks. In the coordinates [def-trf-etale-presented-recovery-coordinates], the generator-normalized free comparisons are isomorphisms, each $d_i$ has a unique Zariski lift $h_i$, and there are quasi-coherent cokernels $F_i$ [pqf-def-coherent] with quotient maps and isomorphisms $L_{U_i}F_i\simeq G|_{U_i}$ commuting with those quotients. Each $F_i$ has a linear tensor-section comparison whose unit is the identity on every open. This is precisely the datum EtalePresentedLocalRecovery; no overlap maps or global module are claimed.

proof.text: Put $A_i=\mathcal O_{V_i}^{(K_i)}$ and $B_i=\mathcal O_{V_i}^{(J_i)}$, with coproducts taken in module sheaves. On each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] with $n=1$ makes the structure module quasi-coherent. The affine-local definition [pqf-def-coherent] therefore makes $\mathcal O_{V_i}$ quasi-coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-coproduct-closure], $A_i$ and $B_i$ are quasi-coherent for arbitrary small $K_i,J_i$. By [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom], $L_{V_i}$ preserves these coproducts and sends the structure module to the etale structure module; hence it canonically identifies $L_{V_i}A_i,L_{V_i}B_i$ with the two free modules in the specified presentation.

source.place: Tag 03DX, proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent, proof of (2) by the same construction as (1).

proof.text: Apply the Hom bijection of [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom] to $A_i,B_i$. It gives a unique $h_i:A_i\to B_i$ with image $d_i$ under the identifications of step 1. Define $q_i:B_i\to F_i=\operatorname{Coker}(h_i)$. The module $F_i$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-closure]. Since $L_{V_i}$ preserves cokernels by [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom], both $L_{V_i}q_i$ and the supplied presentation projection are cokernels of $d_i$. Their universal properties give the unique isomorphism $b_i:L_{V_i}F_i\simeq G|_{(V_i)_{\mathrm{et}}}$ commuting with those projections.

proof.text: Use the linear, unit-normalized tensor comparison of lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom on each local cokernel. All contexts contain only proof fields and hence agree by proof irrelevance. This gives localTensor, local_linear and local_unit.

lean.statement: theorem etalePresented_localCokernels (c : ∀ X : Scheme.{u}, ZariskiEtaleModuleContext X) (T : Scheme.{u}) (G : SmallEtaleModules T) (I : Type w) (U : I → T.Etale) (K J : I → Type u) (d : ∀ i, SheafOfModules.free (R := smallEtaleModuleRing (U i).left) (K i) ⟶ SheafOfModules.free (J i)) (q : ∀ i, SheafOfModules.free (R := smallEtaleModuleRing (U i).left) (J i) ⟶ (presentedEtaleRestriction (U i)).obj G) (zero : ∀ i, d i ≫ q i = 0) (presentation : ∀ i, Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ (q i) (zero i)))) : Nonempty (EtalePresentedLocalRecovery c T G I U K J d q)
